subject: How do you send variables from shinyserver to shinyUI

messages.author: 0e160dfcf4cca382
messages.subject: How do you send variables from shinyserver to shinyUI
parts:
I have a csv file(containing a range of datestamps) that I'm reading in and doing some processing on within shinyserver. I have a function defined that obtains the minimum and maximum datestamp. I somehow need to be able to pass that information to shinyUI to define the minimum and maximum possible date that can be selected in a dateRangeInput widget. What i'm trying to do specifically is:

library(shiny)

shinyServer (function(input,output, session) {

minmaxTimes <- reactive(function(){

dataframe <- read.csv(file=sample.csv, header=TRUE, sep=",")
minTime = floor_date(min(dataframe$Time),"minute")
maxTime=ceiling_date(max(dataframe$Time),"minute")
value<-c(minTime, maxTime)
return(value)
}


I need to some how pass "value" to the UI for use in the dateRangeInput() widget 


shinyUI(
fluidPage(
.......
.......
......
......
           dateRangeInput("date", label="Date:", start=minmaxTimes() [1], end=minmaxTimes()[2], min=minmaxTimes()[1], max=minmaxTimes()[2], startview="month"),

.......
.......
......

))

obvious, this would not work but is there anyway to do this without having to read in the CSV file outside of shinyserver?
Help is greatly appreciated!

messages.author: ec79ef2df02af517
messages.subject: Re: How do you send variables from shinyserver to shinyUI
parts:
Hi Daniel,

You could try reading the CSV file into the application as part of a separate file called global.R

See the Global Objects section here:

http://rstudio.github.io/shiny/tutorial/#scoping

In short, do your calculations in the global.R file, then include the source path in ui.R. e.g.

source("pathtofile/global.R", local=T)

Then reference the variables as usual.

Hope that helps.

Cheers
Phill

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: How do you send variables from shinyserver to shinyUI
parts:
By using the updateXXX functions, you can keep all of your UI in ui.R which I personally think is easier to read and work with. It also means that the UI can load and re-load faster because all of the UI is just sent once when the page is rendered, rather than over the websocket connection both on startup and when something changes.

That said, there are plenty of situations where you have truly dynamic UI and you just need to use renderUI.
